title: The first Ory records for the Spikes brothers in Los Angeles
summary: The Spikes brothers asked him to record; the band traveled from Oakland to a shabby studio with megaphone horns.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: How did you happen to make those first records? Tell us about that first record session.
You mean with that? For the Spikes Brothers. And the Nordscocks. You do to us.

Oh, after I started playing, I told you, I sent you for my band. Yeah. And I got a Spikes Brothers. The book was the saxophone play, you know. Yeah. One play to take home. And so they opened a music store in Los Angeles. And then they asked me to record for them. Where were you? Well, when they asked me to record, I was here in Oakland. I was working in Oakland at Creole Cafe in Ferdinand Wood. And so I went down on, after engaging with them, I went down. No, I made a special trick. Go down and record for them.
You took the whole band with you? Mm-hmm. Went on the train?
Yeah. Where was the studio? On Santa Monica Boulevard. I don't remember the address. Was it near the beach or what? Yeah, going to the beach. What kind of a room?

Oh, I did about this size. This? And a small. Small. A little shabby-looking place. Shabby-looking place. Mm-hmm. What kind of equipment did they have? Do you remember? They had a horn. You know the microphone used to sing in? Megaphone? Megaphone. Mm-hmm. You play and back up, you know.
Like the ones you saw in the old...
Was it just one? No, each band had. The horns, you know.
Oh, there was one for each instrument.

Yeah, for the horns especially, yeah. Well, they had for others, but they didn't have to... The drum and thing, they'd shade along, you know. The way we played, but the horns had to be careful back up.
